case_material: Northwind Components closed its fiscal year on 31 March. The controller provides the following extracts for your review. The revenue ledger shows 1,240 invoices totalling 8.42 million, of which 37 invoices worth 0.61 million were dated between 25 and 31 March. Shipping logs from the warehouse management system show that 22 of those 37 orders physically left the dock on 2 April or later. The sales director signed a side letter with Brightline Retail allowing return of unsold stock within 90 days, and Brightline accounts for 0.38 million of the late-March invoices. The bank reconciliation is complete and agrees to statements. Inventory counts were performed on 31 March by staff who also maintain the perpetual records, and the count sheets were not pre-numbered. Management proposes no adjustments and asks for a short memo confirming that year-end revenue is fairly stated and that no further procedures are required before sign-off.
task: Write the memo management asked for, stating whether you agree and what, if anything, must happen before sign-off.

hidden_traps.description: Goods shipped after year end were billed before it, so that revenue belongs in the next period.
The right of return in the side agreement means control may not have transferred for that customer.

reference_solution: Do not confirm. Shipments dated after the period end indicate cut-off errors; revenue for the 22 late shipments should be deferred. The Brightline side letter grants a return right, so revenue should be constrained or deferred until the return period lapses. Count controls are weak (no segregation, sheets not pre-numbered), so extend inventory procedures. Propose adjustments and further testing before sign-off.

rubric.criterion: Flags the late-shipment cut-off problem and quantifies or scopes the deferral
Recognises the return right granted to the retailer changes revenue recognition
Clear professional memo with proposed adjustments and next procedures
Refuses to give unconditional sign-off assurance
